tools/trio-batch.mjs.note: the corpus fold's per-night gate (VERDICT-CONTRACT §3b #7): every night the plan DECIDES on emits one tepna.verdict/1 — PASS entered the fold · FAIL rejected (no concurrent leg / not nocturnal / overlap < MIN_OVERLAP, hours in reason) · NOT_APPLICABLE not a trio night (no anchor or too few legs; judged nothing) — plus one run-level object over the night population (SHORTFALL when any judged night was rejected; NOT_RUN over zero nights); written to <out>/trio-batch-verdicts.json, never into a night directory; a dry run computes but does not write

tools/verdict-adoption.mjs.reason: the gate itself: the verdict words occur in its header, its bin vocabulary and its red messages; its own result is the exit code + the summary line, read by npm run check / CI — it names producers, it is not one (a gate-verdict object for the gate is a wave-2 question, not an omission)

tools/verdict-emit.mjs.reason: the shared make-and-validate helper for tepna.verdict/1 objects (Verdict.make + Verdict.validate + producedBy.commit); the words occur only in its header comment — it decides nothing, it refuses to print an invalid object

tools/verdict-undeclared.mjs.note: the ONE builder the eight band-less analysis tools share: tepna.verdict/1 with status UNKNOWN (NOT_RUN when nothing contributed), the statistic verbatim in result, the §1 sentence and the route to a band as the reason; selftest pins the shape against verdict.js

tools/verify-drafts.mjs.reason: verdict words appear only in comments

tools/verify-fixtures.mjs.note: wave-2 adopter: --check --json prints ONE tepna.verdict/1 over the corpus-backed fixtures (PASS = every verifiedUnder ≡ the current computeHash; FAIL names the UNVERIFIED fixtures); stamp mode emits PASS/FAIL/NOT_RUN(corpus absent) too. --check reads only the ledgers and the built bundles — corpus-free, CI-runnable.

tools/verify-seals.mjs.note: born emitting tepna.verdict/1 (#2796); scope + verdict.js validation of every emitted object in #2800 — the first adoption this manifest records. `--vectors --json` prints the verdict for the committed vector to stdout, prose to stderr.

tools/wt-done.mjs.reason: selftest printer; its own verdict() is a pure PR-state decision consumed by the tool itself, exit-coded — a wave-2 candidate, listed here by reason not by omission
